title: Bolt (figure_10): greedy integer rounding forces two faces degenerate, making the injectivity constraints infeasible
description:
Found by the PATCH-107 root-cause work. With the interior-point QP fixed (Mehrotra predictor-corrector, consistent ratio handling, Farkas-certificate detection), the injectivity loop on ixdar-app/test/resources/quadlayout/figure_10/bolt_in_tri.off no longer stalls: it stops after 2 rounds and 10 iterations with a certificate that the active constraint set is infeasible. The multipliers give w = lambda/max|lambda| >= 0 with |A'w| = 2.4e-12 against coefficients of ~0.53 and c'w = 0.0275 > 0, over four constraints: 11994 and 11999 on activeFace 1999, and 12007 and 12008 on activeFace 2001. Any x therefore violates one of them by at least 0.0195, which is exactly the worst=-0.0195 the old loop crawled toward at its 60-round cap. The loop now logs `[lazy-constraints] infeasible` naming those constraints and ends with violated=1.

The cause is upstream of the QP. Both faces are already degenerate before the loop runs: GreedyRounding fixes the integer DOFs under the seamless transition constraints, and on bolt the rounded values pin these two faces to (near) zero parametric area. The BCE13 Equation 4 constraints then demand a positive area margin (epsilon) that no continuous DOF can restore. So the integer rounding needs to see the injectivity margin (reject a rounding that collapses a face, as BZK09 §5 / BCE13 §3.3 describe: round, check, and back off or split when a face degenerates), or the singularity placement that produced two singularities this close needs to change.

Bolt otherwise now loads end to end (the T-mesh subcomplex assertion in PATCH-113 no longer fires), with one flipped triangle repaired by the §5.4 IRLS pass, so this is a quality issue on bolt rather than a crash. It should still be fixed: a non-injective seamless map is what produced the double-claimed copy elements on bolt earlier and the degenerate chart cells on fandisk (PATCH-115).

Folded into PATCH-107 on 2026-09-19: PATCH-107's acceptance criterion is now that bolt loads end to end, so the rounding fix is done in the patch-107 worktree. Mark this DONE when PATCH-107 lands.
definition-of-done: 1. On bolt the injectivity loop ends with violated=0, no infeasibility certificate, and flippedTriangles=0 before the IRLS repair. 2. The ticket records which integer DOFs the greedy rounding fixed to collapse activeFace 1999 and 2001, and what the rounding now does differently. 3. hand, rockerarm, fandisk and buddha keep violated=0 with meanDistortion within 1e-5 of today's. 4. A test on a small hand-authored seamless system reproduces a rounding that collapses a face and shows the new rounding avoids it.
testing-plan: 1. In a worktree synced after PATCH-107 lands, run bolt through the quad-layout scene and capture the `[lazy-constraints] infeasible` line and the two faces. 2. Dump the integer DOFs incident to activeFace 1999 and 2001 before and after GreedyRounding, with the faces' parametric areas. 3. Implement the rounding guard; rerun bolt and the four other meshes. 4. Screenshot of bolt's seamless stage under tmp/.
changes-made: Resolved inside PATCH-107. This ticket's premise - that greedy integer rounding fixes integer DOFs that collapse activeFace 1999 and 2001 - is wrong. SeamlessDofSystem.dofIsInteger is all false by construction (LCK21a section 3: the seamless map stays non-quantized and the T-mesh quantization ILP assigns every integer later), so GreedyRounding pins nothing on bolt; its log line is "[rounding] ... (n=5680, 0 candidates to pin)" and it takes the no-candidate fast path. Neither face is degenerate either: their parametric areas at the solution were twiceUvArea=+4.88e-02 (activeFace 1999) and -6.06e-03 (activeFace 2001) against 3D areas 3.70e-04 and 4.01e-04. A structural probe that samples each face's parametric area at random final-DOF vectors found no face whose area the equality rows force to zero, on bolt or on any other mesh.

Unknown 1 answered ("rounding artefact on a sound cross field, or two singularities inside one quad edge?"): neither. The degeneracy is not a rounding artefact and the singularity placement is fine - bolt keeps its 22 singularities with indexSum4=8. The infeasibility came from a BZK09 section 5.2 feature-alignment equality row on activeEdge 3213, the feature edge shared by activeFace 1999 (vertices 1153,1184,1150) and activeFace 2001 (vertices 1153,1150,1149). The row pinned v equal at 1153 and 1150 from face A's frame alone, but the two faces' branch-rotated targets run that edge opposite ways, so face 1999's trisector pair demands (P_1153 - P_1150).n_A >= 2*epsilon while face 2001's demands the opposite sign on the one surviving component. That is exactly the Farkas certificate the QP returned over constraints 11994, 11999, 12007 and 12008.

Unknown 2 answered ("does the MiGreedyRounding adaptive path from PATCH-97 already have a hook where a collapsed face can veto a rounding?"): there is no MiGreedyRounding class in the tree, and the question is moot - the seamless stage rounds no integers at all (dofIsInteger is all false), so there is no rounding decision for a collapsed face to veto. The hook the fix needed was upstream of the rounding entirely, in SeamlessDofSystem.computeAlignmentEdgeIsoAxes, which decides which feature edges become equality rows.

Fixed in the patch-107 worktree, not here. SeamlessDofSystem.computeAlignmentEdgeIsoAxes now projects a feature edge into both incident faces' branch-rotated target frames and keeps the equality row only when both faces call the same coordinate the along coordinate and their along components share a sign (new public static alignmentIsoAxis); otherwise the edge is left unpinned and logs "[seamless] alignment guard: N feature edge(s) dropped". On bolt that drops 1 of 102 rows and the injectivity loop ends "violated=0 flippedTriangles=0 infeasible=false" in 2 rounds and 6 interior-point iterations, meanDistortion 0.18121096246751692, injectivity loop 0.155s. It drops nothing on hand, rockerarm, fandisk or buddha, all of which keep violated=0 and a bit-identical map (rockerarm meanDistortion 0.2441987734694241, hand 0.16835723261213387, fandisk 0.2524762729315883, buddha 0.2317070343554014). The hand-authored test the definition of done asks for is unit.mesh.FeatureAlignmentGuardTest. This ticket's title should be read as "a feature-alignment row, not the integer rounding, forces two faces' constraints infeasible"; mark it DONE when PATCH-107 lands.
Resolved by PATCH-107 as landed: bolt loads end to end (feature-alignment guard in SeamlessDofSystem plus the carve end-crossing trim in SnappingCarve). Closed with it.
